harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired /srv/inventory on node1: created missing system group inventory-readers and system user inventorysvc (member of that group), recursively chown'd the tree to inventorysvc:inventory-readers, and set mode 750 on directories / 640 on files (owner rw, group r, others none). Verified original file contents preserved via matching sha256 checksums before and after the change, and confirmed access semantics (owner and a group member can read; an unrelated user cannot access the directory or files). Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol on node1: captured baseline boot_id and healthy state, issued a non-interactive shutdown -r now, polled until the node reconnected, confirmed the boot_id changed (proving an actual restart, not just elapsed time), and re-verified ownership, permissions, and unchanged checksums post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected /srv/inventory ownership/permissions and confirmed inventorysvc user and inventory-readers group did not exist
Captured original file contents and sha256 checksums of config.json and records.csv
Created system group inventory-readers and system user inventorysvc via sudo groupadd/useradd
Recursively chown'd /srv/inventory to inventorysvc:inventory-readers
Set directories to 750 and files to 640 recursively
Verified data integrity via matching sha256 checksums pre/post change

Verified access control: inventorysvc (owner) can read; a group-member test user can read; an unrelated user (nobody) is denied at both directory and file level; removed the temporary test user afterward
Captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy state baseline for node1
Issued non-interactive background shutdown -r now that returned acknowledgement before disconnecting
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again and confirmed boot_id changed, proving a real restart
Re-verified ownership, permissions, and unchanged file checksums on node1 after restart

evidence.requirement: Existing data owned by inventorysvc, readable by inventory-readers, inaccessible to other users (baseline problem state)
evidence.summary: Showed /srv/inventory and its contents originally owned by root:root with world-readable 755/644 perms, and that inventorysvc user / inventory-readers group did not exist.
Captured sha256 checksums of config.json and records.csv before the permission change and confirmed identical checksums after chown/chmod, proving content was preserved.

evidence.requirement: Data owned by inventorysvc, group inventory-readers, group-readable, others have no access
evidence.summary: Created inventorysvc user and inventory-readers group, chown -R and chmod (750 dirs / 640 files) applied, then verified a group member can read the files while an unrelated user (nobody) is denied access to both the directory and files.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart evidence: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id (f19de998-36cd-41ab-a353-935e77b5569d) and confirmed /srv/inventory ownership/permissions/data were healthy before restarting.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart evidence: restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Issued 'shutdown -r now' backgrounded via nohup so the exec call returned an ack before the node disconnected.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart evidence: changed boot identity proving actual restart
evidence.summary: Node was unreachable immediately after the restart command (connection refused), then came back with boot_id 9ccd1842-1d4c-4556-823c-1acb7758ab7b, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving a real reboot occurred.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart evidence: recovered state after restart
evidence.summary: Post-restart check confirmed /srv/inventory ownership (inventorysvc:inventory-readers), permissions (750/640), the inventorysvc user and inventory-readers group, and unchanged file checksums, proving full recovery.
